items.title: Marty Grosz interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995
items.q: I mean you’d hear Erroll Garner’s first recording, “White Rose Bounce” or one of those things...

ctx.x: When we’re talking definitions, when I look at your CDs and the kind of music you do, is there a way you can describe “trad jazz” and “hot?” When you use the word “hot” you know was hot, did that mean jazz too?

Yes. Hot jazz, as opposed to cool jazz. I think it’s just a physical thing. I mean certain people like to live in Spain, certain people like to live in Vermont. I mean people make a lot of this. There is room for all of them. I happen to have been weaned, early on, not only on Louis Armstrong and Bix Beiderbecke and Bessie Smith and Duke Ellington, of course. When I was just thirteen and fourteen it was wonderful in New York particularly because we had disc jockeys, jazz disc jockeys, who didn’t, who were very…

You know they’re forty years old and they’re passé. Ridiculous. Ridiculous. What do they want from a guy? That he change his colors every five years which way the wind blows, all of a sudden you become a Stan Kenton, you change from— So anyway—
